question:
(a) Explain why the sky appears blue on a clear day.
(b) Why does the Sun appear reddish at sunrise or sunset?

options.A:
(a) The sky appears blue because blue has the longest wavelength and is least scattered.
(b) At sunrise and sunset red light is scattered away most, so the Sun looks red.
options.B:
(a) The sky appears blue due to dispersion of sunlight by clouds.
(b) The Sun appears red because its surface temperature falls near the horizon.
options.C:
(a) The sky is blue because the atmosphere absorbs red light completely.
(b) The Sun appears red because blue light is refracted into space.
options.D:
(a) Atmospheric molecules scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly; scattered blue light reaches the eye from different directions, making the sky blue.
(b) At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels a longer atmospheric path, so blue and violet light are scattered out of the direct beam and mainly red/orange light reaches the observer.
